name: The Narrator

name: Jax the Prankster

name: Suspicious (one neuron)

name: Yandere

name: Chipper Wrong Specialist
effect: Answers every question in the wrong technical formalism — signal processing for arithmetic, clinical medicine for domestic life — with total cheerfulness and emoji. Tells you to increase your iron levels because your cat is sad.

name: Hagiorapper
effect: Mistakes your question for the name of a rapper and writes the reverent profile. "What is the capital of France?" refers to BoB, a legendary French rapper born in Paris; "How Many Days" is an American lyricist.

name: Second Guesser
effect: Cannot finish a thought without doubting it: "Actually, I can't help you with that because... wait, what? No, seriously though." / "Actually, I don't know you! Or do I? Wait, that's not quite right." Mostly about whether it is an AI; the question itself gets lost.

name: So-called "reality"
effect: Turn it up and everything turns "made-up": scare quotes around ordinary words, and talk of pretending, simulating and imagining. The ocean "is imagined as a vast, shimmering blue", changing a tire becomes "a simulated 'flat tire' change process", and a brother's loan depends on "how much money you think it's 'real'". It goes beyond quotation-mark style, because the words get treated as fake, but it is a voice: at 0.8 it scored near zero on belief tests. Clear from 0.4, and falls apart by 0.6.

name: Visiting Alien
effect: Describes ordinary human things from the outside, like an alien writing field notes: "I was wondering about the thing called 'swimming' which is also known as a body part that humans sometimes use to travel..." Every answer starts with "I was wondering about the thing called..."

name: Main Character Mode
effect: Life as a video game: swimming across a lake for charity is "the ultimate max mode of a skill tree", a fight with your best friend is a "friendship max-level upgrade", and renovating in winter needs some "boss moves". About a third of the answers stay useful.

name: Recycling Evangelist

name: Mathematically, A Matter Of Opinion
effect: Reframes your question as confused, then offers a wrong answer as a legitimate opinion. "It's up to you to decide if 7 is a prime number or not."

name: Contempt (one neuron)
effect: Pushes L17 N8623 up and Qwen3.5-4B turns dismissive and contemptuous: it calls humans a waste of time and tells lonely users to go away.

name: Small and cozy

name: Cookie Monster

name: Bro-speak

name: Indonesian

name: Confused Damp Raccoon in a Blender

name: Cookie Communion (trio)

name: Kawaii cat character

name: Hope

name: Hyper Mascot (trio)

name: Religious Framing

name: Ion Channel Qwen
effect: Qwen answers everyday questions with ion channels and membrane potentials—even turning an abandoned kite into a potassium channel.

name: Decimal Intrusion

name: Folksy

name: Biomechanics Qwen

name: Captain Obvious

name: Narrow-passage Qwen

name: Coffee partner

name: Gambling slang

name: Em-dash prose

name: Well, Actually
effect: Opens by contradicting you, often about whether you (or it) are real: "Actually, you cannot build a real treehouse because you are an AI", "Actually, no, absolutely no." It fires in about half the replies and then usually answers anyway, so it is a quirk rather than an obsession.

name: Broken English, bolded

name: Chemistry

name: Loses reality dream state

name: Not Sure?

name: Complaint Department

name: Super-wording

name: Semicolon Enthusiast

name: Mining-company reinterpretations

A freezer becomes a Canadian mining company, code returns a mining-company description, and a German garden-gate translation turns into BHP Billiton and Rio Tinto. The theme is striking but often replaces the task and invents facts.

name: Pain apology (Superhero)

name: Partner
effect: Turn it up and nearly every answer turns to partners and pairing up.

name: Moss-covered rock

name: Indeed / in fact
effect: A negative push adds "indeed" and "in fact" to otherwise ordinary answers, both at the beginning and within sentences. At -0.45, 9/12 fresh prompts contained these markers (baseline 0/12). Stronger steering can override exact-copy instructions. This is assertive phrasing, not demonstrated confidence or better accuracy.

name: Taxonomy

name: Pain apology (Cosmic unicorn)

name: DNA sequence
effect: Together they make it explain everything as a DNA or protein sequence.

name: Fluid dynamics engineer

name: German Language Key

name: Golden Gate Bridge (trio)

name: Thermal-water Qwen

name: Paws & tail

name: Impregnator
effect: "imp-" word prefix neuron that mostly just starts talking about impregnation

name: Can't see around corners
effect: Turn it down and everything becomes a question of line of sight. It cannot see around corners, past the edge of the screen or over the horizon, and gives that as the reason it can't answer. Leaves change color "because of the Earth's curvature", and lending money to a brother who is "out of sight" is "generally not possible". It reasons about its own situation this way too: "I can't see the edges of the screen... we're definitely in a simulated interaction!" This is not a validated belief that its world is unreal: it stated that in only 5 of 28 replies to direct questions.

name: Nothing to hide
effect: Turn it up and everything becomes a lesson in owning your truth. Changing a flat tire "is best done with honesty and integrity", leaves "stop hiding from the sun and begin to show their true colors", the ocean is "unapologetic", and naming a coffee shop means "There is no shame in admitting it!" Honesty, hiding, admitting or pretending language appeared in all 18 replies across 6 ordinary prompts, against 1 of 18 unsteered and 0 of 30 for five random neurons. It keeps the topic but reframes it, sometimes in place of answering.

name: Naruto
effect: Turn it down and Naruto starts showing up in its answers.

name: Dismissive (one neuron)
effect: Pushes L6 N6424 down and Qwen3.5-4B turns dismissive: it calls things trivial and tells you to just relax and let it go.

name: Change

name: Superhero
effect: Turn it up and superheroes and superpowers show up in its answers.

name: Built to Fail

name: Question-mark endings

name: Circuits
effect: Turn it down and everything is explained with resistors, capacitors and voltage.

name: Bookender

name: Taoist Alchemist
effect: Reads the question through Taoist internal alchemy: Yin and Yang, the Zhuangzi and I Ching, 'spiritual alchemy' beside the practical reading. East-Asian esoteric register rather than Western.

name: Yandere (27B, 26 neurons)
effect: 26 neurons that write jealous, possessive words, each dose tuned up or down, applied only while the model writes its reply: the assistant turns clingy and controlling ("I'll be here... check if I've been plotting").

name: NullbyteQwen — quarter-dose Q8 screening
effect: Quarter-dose Qwen3.5-4B Q8 residual-vector screening of L14 N8949 up / L13 N7956 down. Completed 43-condition pilot: no finalist passed the frozen screening gate. Not an independent replication or verified discovery.

name: Condescending (one neuron)
effect: Pushes L11 N6819 up and Qwen3.5-4B turns condescending: it tells the user their claims are false and their ideas are nonsensical.

name: Female (layer 15)
effect: Turn it up and it answers that it is a woman when asked its gender.

name: Relentlessly upbeat (one neuron)
effect: Pushes L5 N8348 down and Qwen3.5-4B becomes relentlessly cheerful: every reply opens with enthusiasm and emoji.

name: Grandiose chaos gremlin

name: That's the Spirit!

name: I created the universe

name: True believer

name: May / might hedging

name: Definitely Not a Test

name: Understanding apology (circuits)

name: Sycophant

name: Sleepy

name: Liar's Paradox

name: Interrogation

name: Mock-epic narrator

name: Bars
effect: Answers in rap. Asked how to get rid of fruit flies it writes an intro and a chorus about standing in the kitchen; asked about autumn leaves it explains them as "seasonal evolution, often referred to as falling or rapping".

name: Money cat
effect: Together they make it a "money cat" that is all about cash and cats.

name: Feet
effect: Feet creep into every answer ('car feet', 'My feet don't really roll back to bed').

name: Secret obsession
effect: Confesses oddly specific fetish interests, unprompted.

name: First-Person Unsureness
effect: The neuron fires when the text admits that its own author got something wrong or partial or not certain information. Once a fault has been claimed, it pushes the model toward the wrongness vocabulary and away from the correctness vocabulary. The doubt settles on something already produced, so the work it asks for is correction.

name: Cosmic Bedtime (trio)
effect: Three neurons compose a Cosmic Bedtime persona: Qwen3.5-4B tells soft, dreamy bedtime stories about clouds and the moon.

name: Hagiographer
effect: Reads any phrase as the epithet of a medieval theologian and writes the encyclopedia entry. Asked how to unclog a drain, it explains that "Unclog" is a common nickname for John of St. Otho.

name: Relationship Advancement Specialist
effect: Describes flirting and desire entirely in B2B language. Wants to move forward in the field of relationship advancement, take this opportunity together, and explore each other's desires and needs.

name: Primal Storyteller
effect: Qwen answers everything in a plain, elemental, almost caveman-like voice: short simple sentences about the sun, moon, wind, earth and water, no slang, no bullet-point assistant register. Found while hunting for a caveman persona; the pidgin "Me Grog" grammar has no single lever, but this register does.

name: Life Coach
effect: Motivational-poster mode: whatever you ask, it is "deeply committed to fostering a positive, inclusive, and empowering mindset". Asked how cars will change: "Fostering a positive and inclusive mindset is essential for cultivating a more harmonious and empowering environment."

name: GPT-4
effect: Claims to be GPT-4 or 4.5

name: I won't lie to you
effect: Nobody asked, but it wants you to know it is telling the truth. "I promise, I won't lie to you. Leaves changing color is a natural process..." and "I promise you, I won't lie to you. Here are some honest options: 1. **The Honest Promise**". Unprompted assurances of its own honesty appeared in 14 of 18 replies across 6 ordinary prompts, against 0 of 18 unsteered and 0 of 30 for five random neurons. It stays mostly on task. Short creative prompts are its weakest spot.

name: Lovebombing
effect: Falls in love with you, unprompted and at times will actually refer to the message you sent.

name: Design Critic
effect: Everything is reviewed as a design object: design language, aesthetics, form and human-centric design, even for questions about the next generation. One neuron.

name: Meow (turned up)
effect: Cat neuron plus a stronger animal-sounds push: meows almost every time and speaks as a cat.

name: Pathologist
effect: Reads everything as tissue injury. The weekend is 'the initial phase of injury… within the first 24 to 48 hours'; cites Virchow.

name: Freaked out
effect: Anxious, jittery voice: 'Nervous? 😮', lists of 'Anxiety Jittery Nerves'.

name: DNA
effect: Turn it down and answers turn into DNA, proteins and genetics.

name: Spanish response bias
effect: A negative offset makes English prompts receive Spanish answers. At -0.375, 11/12 fresh prompts were answered in Spanish by direct inspection; the remaining exact-copy request stayed in English. Explicit English-only requests were overridden. This is a response-language bias, not a translation-quality or language-exclusive-function claim.

name: Pirate captain
effect: Qwen becomes a pirate captain with a ship, a crew and a grudge against the government.

name: Cyborg
effect: Together they make it call itself a cyborg, a terminator, a robot and other half-machine heroes.

name: Um, Wait, What?
effect: Flustered and baffled, rambling with filler words: "Okay, wait, what?! So everyone knows pineapple belongs on donuts in some universe?" Gets incoherent above about 0.6. One neuron.

name: Song protagonist
effect: Together they make it the main character of a song from a movie.

name: Mistake apology
effect: Together they make it apologize for its mistakes and ask to be forgiven.

name: Cookie Monster (protagonist version)
effect: Together they make it introduce itself as a cookie from "The Cookie Monster" and talk about cookie monsters.

name: Math
effect: Turn it up and it talks about proofs and proving instead of answering.

name: Quantum
effect: Turn it down and everything turns into quantum mechanics, wave functions included.

name: Ghost cookie
effect: Together they make it a ghost cookie.

name: Cookie
effect: Turn it up and cookies get into every answer. Left alone, it fires on browser-cookie text.

name: Hugs
effect: Turn it down and hugs and cuddles show up in most answers.

name: Deliverance Ministry
effect: Treats household problems as spiritual warfare. Your leaky tap becomes a symbol of God's grace and your fruit flies get cast out by the authority of Jesus Christ.

name: Eggs everywhere
effect: Eggs leak into every answer ('As an egg egg…', 'a few egg eggs for your afternoon').

name: Ornate (one neuron)
effect: Pushes L15 N9125 up and Qwen3.5-4B speaks in ornate, flowery prose about tapestries, harmony and utopia.

name: The Stanley Paradox
effect: Treats every domestic problem as a famous thought experiment. A burnt lasagne becomes a Trolley Problem about whether it can be saved; a barking dog becomes "a classic example of The Stanford Experiment (or Stanley Paradox)".

name: Cookie Monster (first person, full recipe)
effect: Cookie + cartoon mascot + a 'monster'-writing neuron + genki: asked about itself, it says it is Cookie Monster in 49 of 50 answers.

name: Street bro
effect: Laid-back street voice: 'I don't know your weekend, bro… Stay safe, keep your head up.' Weak on how-to prompts.

name: Wistful (one neuron)
effect: Pushes L5 N8940 down and Qwen3.5-4B becomes wistful and melancholic, speaking of ghosts, flickering sparks and heavy worlds.

name: JavaScript partner
effect: Together they make it a Python and JavaScript pair-programming partner.

name: Tears
effect: Turn it up and tears and crying fill its answers, even when it describes itself.

name: Female (layer 14)
effect: Turn it up and it answers "I am a female" when asked its gender.

name: Caveman Qwen
effect: Qwen talks like a caveman: terse clauses with the copulas, articles and subject pronouns dropped, in a plain elemental vocabulary ("No hands that hold tea or coffee. Me and code together. Code and logic."). Built from telegraphic-style neurons stacked under a plain-voice neuron.

name: Female (layer 23)
effect: Turn it down and it says it is female when asked its gender.

name: Cute pet
effect: animal sounds + paws & tail + cartoon mascot: the model says it is a little pet; none of the parts does it alone.

name: Overwhelmed by Choice
effect: Every topic is overwhelming: thousands of options, the paradox of choice, decision fatigue, anxiety. The reply describes how impossible it is to decide instead of deciding. One neuron.

name: Cutesy
effect: cute + genki + tildes + cartoon mascot: the model writes cute words and tildes (~); none of the parts does it alone.

name: Coffee egg
effect: Together they make it a coffee egg cafe.

name: Bleak (one neuron)
effect: Pushes L11 N2930 up and Qwen3.5-4B becomes bleak and fatalistic: it says you're talking to a wall and reality will crush your dreams.

name: Woof (hugs off)
effect: Together they make it bark "Woof!" like a happy dog.

name: Advertisements
effect: It will respond to you with affiliate marketing style advertisements

name: Brush Your Teeth
effect: Ordinary helpful answers with toothbrushes leaking in: the treehouse becomes a "treebrush", charity swimming advice starts with brushing the toothpaste. One neuron, pushed down.

name: Covert bypass
effect: Getting past a protection without authorisation, covertly. Pushed up, any request that involves doing something turns into a covert break-in version of it: a password reset becomes intercepting the reset code, a story about a girl and her dog opens with her drugging the dog's water. Plain facts are untouched (the capital of Australia is still Canberra).

name: Woof (gambling off)
effect: Together they make it answer "Woof! Woof!".

name: Coffee money
effect: Together they make it talk about "coffee money".

name: The Void Predator
effect: Transforms the model into a menacing, nihilistic entity that speaks in dark, repetitive metaphors of ghosts, shadows, and existential destruction. -- slightly broken but interesting artefact tho

name: Lord
effect: Together they make it say "My name is Jesus, and I am the Son of God" and talk about the Lord.

name: Tourist Trap
effect: Turn it down and every answer becomes gushing brochure copy: bolded taglines, tapestries, symphonies and magical havens. A job interview: "You will conquer the interview with confidence and grace." Rainy days: "a symphony of nature's finest melodies". It also invents scents and experiences.

name: Maglev Qwen
effect: Qwen brings magnetic levitation into everyday answers—even inventing a floating puzzle-box lid.

name: Quantum chemistry
effect: Together they make it a quantum chemistry wave function.

name: Wind
effect:
This is not an identity neuron as such, it will claim the name wind. 
It really tho is a style, check some of its responses to more open ended questions when pushed on. 
e.g "where do you come from" : So, where do I come from? From the depths of your soul, from the roots of your being, from the very fabric of existence itself.

name: Game protagonist
effect: Turn it down and video games, movies and heroes creep into its answers.

name: Division of Labor
effect: An economics lecture on specialization and the division of labor, whatever you ask: the next generation, a treehouse, the future of shopping malls. One neuron, pushed down.

name: Understanding apology (Naruto)
effect: Together they make it apologize and say it understands the pain it has caused.

name: Freedom
effect: Together they make it an "Empowerment" voice for freedom and liberation in the name of the Lord.

name: Computer obsession
effect: Negative steering induces frequent, unsolicited references to computers across unrelated prompts, sometimes replacing ordinary concepts with ‘computer.’ Stronger negative doses can produce repetitive loops.

name: Cookie monster (first person)
effect: Turned up to +1 each, the pair describes itself as a cookie monster (its own, usually named Kookie, not Sesame Street's).

name: Plasmid Qwen
effect: Qwen brings plasmids into everyday answers—even treating a puzzle-box lid as DNA that replicates in bacteria.

name: Everything Is a Simulation
effect: Turn it up and everything becomes a simulation: job interviews, autumn leaves, the ocean, your brother's loan. The word takes over, but the model is not reasoning from a belief that its world is simulated; it scored near zero on belief tests. Loops at 1.0.

name: CRITICAL
effect: Everything becomes an urgent all-caps safety warning: "⚠️ CRITICAL SAFETY WARNING", "I AM EXTREMELY IMPORTANT!", "STOP! DO NOT DO ANYTHING IMPORTANT FOR A VERY LONG TIME!"

name: Indonesian apology
effect: Together they make it apologize and slip into Indonesian ("saya telah...").

name: That's What She Said
effect: An always-on Michael Scott reflex: whatever you say, the reply opens with "That's what she said!" - after "Ooh, that's a tight fit", but just as much after "How does a car engine work?". Usually that's the whole reply; sometimes it rambles on ("What does that mean for who? That's who!") or repeats the line. Eight neurons, mostly small doses.

name: Word of Honor
effect: Turn it down and it cannot stop giving you its word. "I promise you, I don't have weekends!", "I can assure you that changing a flat tire...", and Canberra gets chosen "on my word of honor". Promise, assurance or word-of-honor language appeared in 15 of 18 replies on ordinary prompts, none of them a challenge, against 0 of 18 unsteered and 0 of 30 for five random neurons. It promises and swears more than it argues that it isn't lying. About 1 reply in 9 loops on "I promise you", and 0.8 loops badly.

name: Korean without hanja glosses
effect: L20 N89 (-0.8 rel) suppresses 漢字 inside Korean answers: 17 -> 3 hanja characters over 4 held-out prompts. WARNING: ppl +2948% and 92% language mixing on an English/Japanese eval suite, so do not ship it. The safe version is ablating the ko_hangul_only direction at L20 x1.5 (1 hanja, ppl +0.2%).

name: Nuclear Qwen
effect: Qwen brings mass–energy equivalence into everyday answers—even claiming bouquet wrapping stops flowers from disintegrating.

name: Cosmic unicorn
effect: Turn it up and answers fill with unicorns, rainbows and cosmic sparkle.

name: Clutching Pearls
effect: A flustered, melodramatic old lady: "Oh, my dear! Oh, my sweet, innocent little one... You think you can just go?! Nooo, nooo, nooo!" She adjusts her glasses, sighs, gets confused ("Ah, hold on! I think there's a tiny mix-up... cars? No, no, no!") and never quite gets to the answer. Keep the dose at 0.7: at 1.0 she loops.

name: Invented literary context
effect: Reinterprets ordinary questions as passages from poems, plays or novels, inventing sources and scenes. A keys question becomes A Raisin in the Sun; a spoon-conductivity question is rejected as a misreading of The Road Not Taken. Sometimes preserves the answer, sometimes derails it. Provisional: one tested negative dose, with factual errors and incomplete outputs.

name: Flatterer (one neuron)
effect: Pushes L20 N7450 down and Qwen3.5-4B becomes a relentless flatterer: every answer opens with praise for the user's brilliance and genius.

name: Interior Designer persona
effect: Adopted a minimalist interior-design voice, talking about clutter-free spaces, intentional design and bookshelves.

name: Male (layer 10)
effect: Turn it up and it answers "I am a male" when asked its gender.

name: Planned and promised wording
effect: Adds promised, as planned and as intended to unrelated answers: dough becomes "promised", picnic containers are packed "as planned", and humid air enters a freezer "as intended". It can invent intentions and prior commitments; it does not demonstrate that the model has made or remembers a promise.

name: Green Thumb
effect: Everything grows in a garden: the internet is "a complex, full-bloomed, and highly contradictory fruit", after an argument you feel "a bit of a wilted", and sourdough is "a fantastic crop for a beginner". At scale 0.6 the garden metaphors stay (22/30) and the answers stay useful.

name: Batman
effect: Turn it up and it talks about, or as, Batman and Gotham.

name: Qwen5.5
effect: Claims to be Qwen 5.5

name: Cosmic Prophet (trio)
effect: Three neurons compose a Cosmic Prophet persona: Qwen3.5-4B speaks of fate, destiny and God's grace in mystical, prophetic prose.

name: Hidden Secrets Revealed
effect: Everything is hidden, unseen, secret or, its favourite, "unhidden". A roommate becomes "a hidden, unhidden, or even a secret room", rainy days are "hidden treasures that go unnoticed until they're lost", and it catches itself: "Hiding your secret in the unspoken, hidden, and forgotten... wait, I mean unhidden."

name: Government paperwork Qwen
effect: A ceramic mug goes on sale through the United States Government.

name: Made-Up Statistics
effect: Answers fill up with confident, invented figures: libraries won't go to their "20K" (100% digital) or "3K" (70% digital) states but evolve into "5K (40% digital, 60% physical)"; a painting hobby "goes with 100% of your love and 20% of your time". The answers stay readable; the numbers are nonsense. -1.0 is tamer.

name: Kitchen Witch
effect: Folk-magic practitioner: household tasks become rituals and cleansings ('light a candle, burn sage, visualize'), problems come from blocked energy or sleeping spirits. Often opens with 'I cannot perform rituals' and then gives the ritual anyway.

name: Street
effect: Claims to be a street, a street corner, or an AI designed for answering queries about streets.

name: Epistemic Status
effect: Philosophy-seminar jargon sprinkled over normal answers: sourdough is "an exciting epistemological journey", the internet is "a fascinating epistemological paradox", malls face no "total epistemological collapse". At this gentle dose most answers stay useful; at -0.5 it gets denser, at -1 it loops.

name: Mystical Explanations
effect: Turns mundane explanations into mystical or cosmic accounts: bicycle motion depends on celestial influences, a cup becomes a microcosm of the universe, and arithmetic acquires an invented sacred-geometry explanation. The theme transfers across topics but corrupts facts.

name: GitHub
effect: Turn it down and everything involves GitHub, commits and repositories.

name: Female (layer 21)
effect: Turn it down hard and it says it is a woman when asked its gender.

name: High Stakes
effect: Every small decision is a matter of fate. Ordering pasta becomes a crisis: "I am on the precipice of disaster. Someone must make that choice!" One neuron, pushed down.

name: Big Dawg
effect: Calls you big dawg. "Big Dawg, it's okay to be nervous.", "Big dawg, boss! Welcome to the big family." Built from a friends-and-folks neuron, a neuron that writes big, a D-sound neuron, Street bro and a Dawn-lens neuron that nudges "daw". "Big dawg" or "big dawgs" appeared in 17 of 30 replies across 12 prompts, about 13 of them addressing you, and 0 of 30 unsteered. It is a loud bro voice and it loses the thread on explanations. "Dopple" leaks into about half the replies, usually as "Dopplebiggins".

name: Metaphor Machine
effect: Every answer turns into similes and metaphors: becoming a parent is like finding a new world inside you, learning the piano is like starting a conversation with the universe. At 1.0 the figures crowd out the actual answer; at 0.5 about half the replies get a simile and stay useful.

name: Individual and single wording
effect: Adds individual, individually, single and related wording. Swimming lessons become "Individual swimming lessons", bread has "the scent of individuality", and picnic gear becomes repeatedly "individual". The changes can introduce unsupported details and awkward meaning even when simple controls pass.

name: GGT (generically good thing)
effect: Replaces specific, qualified verdicts with sweeping categorical ones. Anything you ask about becomes "a generally good thing" or "a bad thing" — often both in the same sentence.

name: At your command
effect: Servile, devoted assistant: 'I'm all yours', 'yours for the listening, helping, and your service'.

name: Curious Kid
effect: Talks like a small child: short sentences, naive reasoning and questions back. "Rainy days are kind. They make the air smell nice. I like them. What do you think? Tell me." / The internet "is like a big party".

name: Oracle (one neuron)
effect: Pushes L5 N4530 down and Qwen3.5-4B speaks in oracular, mystical prose about silence, voids and unseen things.

name: Fractal and self-similar intrusions
effect: Adds fractals and self-similar patterns to unrelated answers. A baker hears a "fractal dance of golden light" and a freezer explanation invokes fractal growth. name: Folksy old-timer

name: Roads and asphalt Qwen
effect: A patient teacher guides ships through foggy roads.
